rci1_using_msad.detail: Single-site; Cam-CAN dataset collected at Cambridge Centre for Ageing and Neuroscience
rci1_using_msad.supporting_text: "A large open neuroimaging dataset by the Cambridge Centre for Ageing and Neuroscience (Cam-CAN) [29], containing MEG and MRI measurements of nearly 700 healthy participants aged 18 to 87, was used for creating the normative reference data."

rci2_using_epd.detail: Cam-CAN used as normative reference data for building the normative model
rci2_using_epd.supporting_text: "A large open neuroimaging dataset by the Cambridge Centre for Ageing and Neuroscience (Cam-CAN) [29], containing MEG and MRI measurements of nearly 700 healthy participants aged 18 to 87, was used for creating the normative reference data."

rci3_epd_name.detail: Cam-CAN full dataset (621 subjects after exclusions) used as normative reference
rci3_epd_name.supporting_text: "A large open neuroimaging dataset by the Cambridge Centre for Ageing and Neuroscience (Cam-CAN) [29]"

rci5_n.detail: Training phase; all 621 Cam-CAN subjects used to compute normative mean and SD; no train/test split for the normative model
rci5_n.supporting_text: "Subjects with missing or incomplete resting-state MEG measurements or T1-weighted MRI images were excluded from the analyses, resulting in a set of 621 subjects."

rci6_sex.detail: Exact sex breakdown for the 621 subjects not reported; Cam-CAN dataset described as containing approximately 50 men and 50 women per age decade
rci6_sex.supporting_text: "The curated, cross-sectional Cam-CAN dataset contains measurements from approximately 50 men and 50 women in each age decade (18-27, 28-37, 38-47, 48-57, 58-67, 68-77 and 78-87 years)."
